ut_shady_crag.blurb: A small Wingate sandstone cragging area in Long Canyon, off Potash Road outside Moab. Thirteen routes here are all trad, running from 5.9 to 5.12, with the bulk of them in the 5.10 and 5.11 range. That makes it a spot for climbers already comfortable on crack and finger-sized gear rather than a place to learn. As the name hints, the wall holds shade through the morning. Off Width City sits around the corner, so a party can switch to a sunnier wall if the shade turns cold.

ut_sunshine_wall_routes.blurb: Thirteen climbs spread over a section of the long Sunshine Wall in Salt Valley, near Moab. The mix is seven sport routes, five trad lines and a single top rope, graded from 5.7 up to one 5.12, with 5.9 the most common grade, so there is something for newer leaders as well as a few harder tests. The sandstone formation runs for a mile or more: the north end is slabbier and uses a blend of bolts and natural gear, while the south end turns steeper and breaks into small towers.

ut_stinky_stash_wall.blurb: A west-facing wall high in Albion Basin, up in Little Cottonwood Canyon at roughly 10,000 feet, near Cecret Lake. The rock is quartzite laced with bands of sandstone, and a few lines carry lichen. The central section is short, about 30 to 50 feet tall, with a handful of bolted lines and a larger set of gear routes. Thirteen climbs, eight trad and five sport, mostly fall between 5.7 and 5.10. Green Stash Wall is around the corner to one side and Cecret Stash on the other. Expect some company, since the neighbouring crags can get busy.

_expect.name: Trad Wall AKA Green River Buttress

ut_trad_wall_aka_green_river_buttress.blurb: A trad-only wall of Wingate sandstone in the Island in the Sky district of Canyonlands, in southeast Utah. All 13 routes are gear climbs between 5.9 and 5.11, and most sit at 5.10, so it appeals to leaders who want steady, mid-grade crack and face climbing. Charlie Horse Needle and Zeus are nearby for those wanting to link a second objective.

ut_upper_tier.blurb: The highest of the tiers at Graveside Matter Wall in Cedar Canyon, near Cedar City. It holds 13 sport routes on steep, featured sandstone, which is regarded as some of the best stone on the wall. Grades start around 5.10 and climb through the 5.11s and 5.12s to one 5.13, so this is a tier for people projecting hard lines rather than warming up. The face gets shade in the morning and sun in the afternoon. Reaching it takes a walk past the slab and along the rim above the Lower Tier.

ut_west_cat_daddy.blurb: The main boulder in the Golden Ladle bouldering area, in the Triassic zone of central Utah, a big, prominent block of gritty sandstone. Thirteen problems range from V3 to V9, with the heart of the grade spread around V4 to V6 and a few harder lines above. Most problems are on the south side. Landings are good, which helps on the slopey top-outs. The parking turnaround is right beside the boulders, so there is almost no walk. The area tends to be quiet, though riders and target shooters sometimes pass through.

ut_tiger_stripe_boulder.blurb: A single boulder in the Secret Garden area, at the bottom of Little Cottonwood Canyon in the central Wasatch. Thirteen problems cover a wide range, from an easy V0 warm-up through mid-grade lines to several very hard problems up in the V11 to V13 band. Secret Garden itself is known for high-quality rock, with classic moderates alongside some of the hardest problems in the canyon, so bring pads and spotters. Access is by a climber's trail leading up from the park-and-ride lot.

_skipped.ut_ren_and_stimpy_wall: Its parent, the Soul Asylum, is marked closed to climbing on the Mountain Project area page; skipped per closed rule.
